newsitem.title: CHINA: GOLDMAN SEES HANG SENG INDEX AT 17,288 AT YR-END.
newsitem.headline: GOLDMAN SEES HANG SENG INDEX AT 17,288 AT YR-END.

text.p: Goldman Sachs said on Thursday that it had upgraded its year-end 1997 target for Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index by 10 percent to 17,288 from 15,800.
That figure would imply a prospective price earnings ratio of 15 times 1998 earnings, a Goldman Sachs research report said.
The U.S. investment bank also said current market liquidity could "well push the Hang Seng Index toward 19,000 prior to the year-end, or 10 percent above our fundamentally based target."

Goldman said its forecast was based on its belief that there was a low probability of a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates following U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's recent Humphrey Hawkins testimony before Congress.
Following the July 23 testimony, Goldman cut its year-end target on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield 70 basis points to 6.60 percent from 7.30 percent.
Goldman also said its recent upgrade on Hong Kong's property development sector to overweight from underweight underpins its confidence in the market outlook.
Above-market interim results from HSBC Holdings are a likely forerunner of a positive results season, it added.
"Interim results by major HSI constituent HSBC on August 4 were above market expectations and are likely to give rise to near-term strength in the Hong Kong market," Goldman said.
Goldman said property developers and stocks with visible China earnings growth remain its top picks.
Its favoured stocks are Citic Pacific, New World Infrastructure, Henderson Land, China Resources Enterprises, Cheung Kong and China Merchants.
